resources.string: Amplifier logo: three ascending audio bars
Start at +6 dB. Reduce the boost if loud audio becomes distorted. The limiter may reduce the actual gain.
Boost paused. Resume to hear the difference.
Global effect is active. Check the sound in your player.
Waiting for a supported player. Restart playback to announce a session.
Android prevented startup. Enable boost again from this screen.
Covers players such as Chrome when supported by your ROM. It may affect other audio on the same mix. Turn this off to test session mode. Only one boost stage is used.
Connect through a player’s Equalizer menu or session announcements. Without either, only a working global mix can boost that player.
Your player opened Equalizer without a usable audio session. Restart playback and reopen Equalizer. If no session is supplied, only a working global mix can boost this player.
Your player supplied an audio session. Use player mode to enable boost on that session and turn off global mix. Other players need their own session connection in this mode.

Exempt Amplifier from battery optimization to help keep audio boost running after you leave the app. Android will ask for your permission.
Notifications: blocked — allow them for quick boost controls
In the video settings, try turning off “Stable volume”. Reels are often mastered louder than streaming videos.

If the sound stays unchanged, open Equalizer in YouTube Music’s settings, if available, and choose Amplifier. Tap “Use player mode” here. An attached global effect does not prove audible gain. Casting and some Bluetooth or offloaded routes may bypass effects.
